title: Toyota to Assemble and Sell Kei Trucks in US
paragraphs: Toyota is bringing a tiny Japanese-style work truck to the United States, and it plans to build the vehicle on American soil.

In November, the carmaker announced that it is reviving Scion, a brand it stopped using about ten years ago. The first vehicle from the new "Scion by Toyota" will be the KEI-01, a small utility truck based on the kei trucks that are common in Japan. In Japan, the same model is sold as the Pixis.

Kei trucks are very small vehicles built to meet Japanese rules on size and engine power. The KEI-01 is just over 11 feet long and less than five feet wide. It has a 660cc three-cylinder engine, a continuously variable transmission and four-wheel drive. It can carry up to 600 pounds, and its cargo bed folds down on three sides to make loading easier.
The truck will be assembled in Indiana, with production set to begin in the second half of 2027. Reports say Toyota will invest $34 million in the project.

However, the KEI-01 will not compete with the large pickups that are popular in the US. It will be classed as a low-speed vehicle, so its top speed will be limited to 25 miles per hour. It will also be right-hand drive, like cars in Japan.

At first, the truck will only be sold to fleet buyers, such as farms, college campuses, towns and delivery businesses, through selected Toyota dealers. Toyota says it may consider limited sales to individual customers later, depending on demand. The price has not been announced.

Kei trucks have become popular with some American farmers and small business owners in recent years. But it is difficult to bring new ones into the country, because vehicles that do not meet US safety standards generally cannot be imported until they are 25 years old. Building the truck locally offers Toyota a way around that problem.
